comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the phenocopy claims (C2, C37-C51) fully supported. OpenEval cites immunofluorescence, TEM, and rescue data; peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a core finding with 'very convincing' evidence.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims about centriole elongation and width (C3, C76-C78). OpenEval cites U-ExM measurements with statistical significance; peer reviewers accept these findings as part of 'well-performed' and 'convincing' quantifications.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims about inner scaffold protein absence (C4, C39, C84-C88, C113). OpenEval and peer reviewers both affirm that compound microtubules are required for inner scaffold formation, with peer reviewers explicitly noting this as a key finding.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims about elongated proximal end proteins (C5, C40, C90-C94, C99). OpenEval describes this as a 'novel architectural defect'; peer reviewers call the cartwheel elongation phenotype 'spectacular' and note it raises questions about size regulation.

Strong agreement with minor caveat. Both support claims about mitotic centriole changes (C6, C103-C106, C126). OpenEval affirms the progression through mitosis; peer reviewers accept the observation but note uncertainty about whether elongation is due to prolonged mitotic duration rather than a direct effect.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims about de novo centriole architecture (C41). OpenEval explicitly addresses this as filling a knowledge gap; peer reviewers implicitly accept through their affirmation of the comprehensive comparative U-ExM data.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims about acetylation and glutamylation (C74, C75, C80-C83). OpenEval affirms the multi-step glutamylation model; peer reviewers accept this as part of the comprehensive characterization showing many aspects of centriole architecture are unaffected.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support localization claims (C9, C53-C57). OpenEval cites multiple imaging approaches as providing strong evidence; peer reviewers affirm the findings as 'convincing' despite acknowledging technical challenges with signal homogeneity.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support computational structure predictions (C68-C71, C73). OpenEval notes high confidence scores and cross-species consistency while acknowledging need for experimental validation; peer reviewers describe the prediction as 'intriguing' without challenging its validity.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims about preserved centriole features (C96-C98, C121-C122). OpenEval notes many assembly processes are independent of compound microtubules; peer reviewers affirm this comprehensive characterization as convincing with detailed quantifications.

Strong agreement with partial overlap. Both evaluations support biochemical interaction and dependency claims. OpenEval focuses on co-IP data (C7, C8, C62-C67); peer reviewers affirm both interactions (C7, C8, C62-C67) and dependency data (C34, C58-C61), describing results as 'convincing' evidence for complex formation.

Partial agreement. OpenEval evaluates interdependency claims (C10, C58-C61) as supported by immunofluorescence and lack of rescue by overexpression. Peer reviewers affirm these claims as part of broader biochemical evidence (R2 covers C58-C61 plus interaction data), describing the complex formation evidence as convincing.

Agreement on overlapping claim. Both evaluations support claims about CEP295 localization and centriole loss mechanism (C100-C102, C125). OpenEval explicitly addresses CEP295 data; peer reviewers implicitly accept through affirmation of comprehensive characterization showing preserved features.
